tool.name: EWAS harmonise arrays
tool.description: combine Illumina 450K and EPIC IDATs into one QC'd matrix without mixing probe chemistry
tool.command: mkdir -p idat out && ## Galaxy stores each IDAT under a numeric dataset id, but minfi resolves ## samples through the Basename column of the sheet, so the original ## _Grn/_Red.idat.gz names have to be restored. #for $pair in $idats ln -s '$pair' 'idat/${pair.element_identifier}' && #end for Rscript '$__tool_directory__/../bin/01_harmonise.R' --sheet '$sheet' --idat_dir idat --out_dir out --detp $qc.detp --detp_frac $qc.detp_frac --drop_sex $qc.drop_sex --bmiq $bmiq --keep_gset TRUE --seed $seed

param.name: sheet
param.label: Sample sheet
param.help: minfi-format sheet plus the longitudinal columns: Sample_Name, Basename, Sentrix_ID, Sentrix_Position, Array_Type (450K or EPIC), Subject_ID, visit, exposure and any time-varying covariates.

param.name: idats
param.label: IDAT collection
param.help: A list containing both the _Grn and _Red IDAT of every sample, from both arrays. Element identifiers must be the original Illumina filenames.

section.name: qc
section.title: Quality control (performed in each array's NATIVE probe space)

param.name: detp_frac
param.label: Maximum fraction of failed probes per sample

param.name: drop_sex
param.label: Drop sex chromosomes
param.help: Sex chromosomes need a sex-stratified model; the downstream stages assume autosomes.

param.name: bmiq
param.label: Apply BMIQ type-I/II correction
param.help: Off by default and normally unnecessary: for all 454,181 probes the two arrays share, Infinium design type, probe sequence and colour channel are 100% concordant, so name-level intersection mixes no chemistry.

tool.help:
**What it does**
Reads 450K and EPIC IDATs, each with its **own** manifest, and produces a single harmonised matrix suitable for a joint longitudinal analysis.
**Order of operations, and why it matters**
Detection p-values, sample QC and background/dye correction are all computed in each array's **native probe space, before any intersection**. Doing QC after merging would judge every EPIC sample on a 450K-shaped probe set and would compute background from a probe panel the sample was never measured on. Merging happens only through ``minfi::combineArrays()``.
**Where the intersection happens**
On CpG **name**, with the manifest resolving bead addresses per array. Measured on ``GPL13534`` and ``GPL21145``: 454,181 CpGs are shared, and for every one of them the bead ``AddressA_ID`` differs between manifests, so an address-level join returns nothing. For those same 454,181 probes the Infinium design type, both probe sequences, colour channel and hg19 position are 100% concordant.
So **harmonisation costs probe content, not chemistry**: 413,745 EPIC-only and 31,396 450K-only probes are dropped, but no shared probe changes design type, and no type-I/II re-typing correction is needed. That is why BMIQ is optional here rather than mandatory.
**Outputs**
Besides the ``GenomicRatioSet`` (which the legacy bump-hunting and block-finding tools require), the tool writes a plain column-major float64 dump of the M-value matrix with a JSON header. The downstream region and block tools read that directly, so no stage needs an R-to-Python bridge.
